name: Mitosis
author: Erin Carter
description: A single dark-liquid cell divides: it necks and snaps into two mirror daughters along one axis, each splitting again along the perpendicular axis into an exact equal-spaced 2x2 quad, then the cascade runs in reverse and all the liquid fuses back to one body — forever, on a palindromic eased phase.

params.label: Cell size
params.effect: Radius of the united mother cell in CSS pixels, scaling the whole genealogy.

params.label: Divide speed
params.effect: How fast the master phase moves through the divide-and-refuse palindrome.

params.label: Wobble
params.effect: Amplitude of the damped ringing after each snap; at zero divisions land without aftershock.
